sections.title: Section B
sections.instruction: Short Answer Questions. Answer each question concisely. (2 marks each)

questions.question: Briefly explain what photosynthesis is and name the part of the plant cell where it primarily takes place.
questions.answer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants and some other organisms use sunlight to synthesize foods with the help of chlorophyll, carbon dioxide, and water. It primarily takes place in the chloroplasts (specifically within the chlorophyll) of plant cells.

questions.question: Describe the gas exchange relationship between photosynthesis and cellular respiration.
questions.answer: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and releases oxygen, while cellular respiration uses oxygen and releases carbon dioxide. These two processes are complementary, forming a cycle where the products of one are the reactants of the other, allowing for the continuous cycling of these gases in an ecosystem.

sections.title: Section C
sections.instruction: Long Answer Questions. Provide a detailed answer for the following question. (5 marks each)

questions.question: Explain the process of photosynthesis. In your answer, include the necessary reactants, the products formed, and why this process is vital for all life on Earth.
questions.answer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy, creating glucose (sugar) for food. The necessary reactants for photosynthesis are carbon dioxide (taken from the air), water (absorbed from the soil), and light energy (captured by chlorophyll). The products formed are glucose (which the plant uses for energy and growth) and oxygen (released into the atmosphere). This process is vital for all life on Earth because it produces the oxygen that most living organisms need to breathe for cellular respiration, and it forms the base of almost all food chains, providing energy to herbivores, and subsequently, to carnivores.
